A1.justification: Both complete, 17-page PDFs describe the same mutual-information-based measurement framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reframing and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements on synthetic ICL and natural-language datasets, generation accuracies, perturbation analyses, and comparisons of human- and LLM-generated texts.

after.justification: v2 reports those empirical results and adds comparisons with other metrics and experiments on eight arithmetic tasks, including task-performance and IE curves.

M1.justification: The macro-minus-micro mutual-information metric, neural estimator and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The rewritten isolated-token example preserves causal isolation, while the full-transformer-output passage clarifies implementation rather than establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original ICL, natural-text and generated-response coverage and adds eight arithmetic tasks: one- and two-digit addition, subtraction, multiplication and division (Section 5.3 and Appendix B). This substantially expands evaluation into explicit arithmetic reasoning.

E2.justification: v2 adds a direct OpenOrca comparison of IE against Exact Match, accuracy and model loss (Section 5.1, Figure 2). This introduces substantial comparative evidence about alternative metrics that was absent from the corresponding evaluation in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include normalized token-to-token metric changes and arithmetic evaluation across eight models spanning approximately 100 million to 20 billion parameters. The arithmetic experiment uses two-shot prompts, default BIG-bench settings and IE averaged over the first five output tokens. The retained experiments keep their previously stated settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds validation analyses testing tokenwise monotonicity and stability against other metrics, and the relationship between IE and arithmetic performance across model sizes (Sections 5.1 and 5.3). The original perturbation ablations, shot-limit and shot-length tests, positional analyses and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report variance bands and Table 1 standard deviations without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added metric comparison uses the existing shaded-variance reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds metric trajectories showing consistently positive IE increments and arithmetic exact-match/IE curves showing strong IE growth at larger model sizes (Figures 2–3). The original ICL and natural-text curves, numerical tables and appendix findings are retained after matching their relocated displays.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit Supervenience Hypothesis 2 and Example 2 deriving E(l)=1, retaining only a brief supervenience footnote. The Markov hypothesis, parity example and central mutual-information formulas remain; the former aggregation equations are expressed equivalently in prose.

C1.justification: v1 presents a theoretical quantification of LLM emergence. v2 explicitly distinguishes Information Emergence from emergent abilities and centers its contribution on quantifying semantic extraction, with claims of semantic faithfulness and sensitivity (Abstract, Sections 1, 2.2 and 7). This changes the intended meaning and scope of the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets IE primarily as semantic determinability and treats its connection to emergent abilities as a limited empirical correspondence. Its expanded limitations explain why varying token positions can undermine interpretability and emphasize sample requirements and restricted evidence for long texts and larger models.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies extraction of complete transformer-block outputs and adds concrete arithmetic prompt templates. However, it omits v1's disclosure that representations are split into 768-dimensional segments and averaged. Estimator hyperparameters, reported runtimes and the code-access destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work shifts substantially from emergence, scaling and ICL toward semantic representation and capability evaluation. v2 adds works such as Apidianaki, Hilpert and Saavedra, PandaLM and JudgeLM, while removing several earlier emergence/scaling references, including Arora and Goyal, Bahri et al., and Wei et al.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around semantic understanding and IE terminology. v2 separates Implementation, Informativeness and Findings, reorganizes the appendices, and places expanded limitations after the conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, adds Figures 2–3, and combines the former ICL and natural-text plots into Figure 4 with revised legends and panel organization. Tables and appendix displays are extensively relocated and resized, including replacing Table 1's text-wrapped placement with a standalone display.

improvement.justification: The clearer distinction between IE and emergent abilities, added metric/arithmetic checks, and more explicit applicability limits improve the paper's interpretability and empirical support. The gain is limited because semantic validity remains indirectly supported, while omission of the 768-dimensional preprocessing detail weakens reproducibility.
